<issue>
Block references broken with incorrect attribute assignment

#### Description

Template block references are not working correctly due to incorrect attribute assignment in the BlockReference constructor. When using `super()` in template blocks or accessing block references, the name and context attributes are swapped, causing AttributeError when trying to access string methods on context objects.

#### Steps/Code to Reproduce

```python
from jinja2 import Environment, DictLoader, Template

# Simple super() usage
env = Environment(loader=DictLoader({
    'base.html': '{% block content %}base content{% endblock %}',
    'child.html': '{% extends "base.html" %}{% block content %}{{ super() }} + child{% endblock %}'
}))
tmpl = env.get_template('child.html')
print(tmpl.render())

# Or with self reference
tmpl = Template('{{ self.foo() }}|{% block foo %}42{% endblock %}|{{ self.foo() }}')
print(tmpl.render())
```

#### Expected Output
```
base content + child
42|42|42
```

#### Actual Output
```
AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'resolve_or_missing'
```

The issue affects any template inheritance or block reference functionality including `super()` calls and `self.block_name()` references.
</issue>
